People: François Guizot (author, Wikidata Q157324), died 1874; Alphonse Marie de Neuville (illustrator, Wikidata Q1494309), died 1885; Robert Black (translator, Wikidata Q7342125), died 1915. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Guizot, François, 1787-1874; Neuville, Alphonse Marie de, 1835-1885 [Illustrator]; Black, Robert, 1830?-1915 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: A popular history of France; from the earliest times, Boston, D. Estes and C.E. Lauriat, 187-?, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/popularhisfrance04guizrich. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 100%, 94%, 94% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Alphonse Marie de Neuville, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
